definition: The practice of constraining a model's generation process in real time (e.g., via grammar constraints or filters) to ensure outputs conform to required formats or safety criteria.
details: Guarded generation techniques include constrained decoding for structured output formats and real-time content filtering, helping ensure outputs are both well-formed and policy-compliant as they are generated.
story: Imagine a new medicine that works brilliantly in the lab but still has to be tested on real people before anyone takes it. Boil it down and it is this: The practice of constraining a model's generation process in real time (e.g., via grammar constraints or filters) to ensure outputs conform to required formats or safety criteria. Here is why it matters: Guarded generation techniques include constrained decoding for structured output formats and real-time content filtering, helping ensure outputs are both well-formed and policy-compliant as they are generated. Rules and red-teaming are the brakes that make the speed trustworthy. That deliberate caution is Guarded Generation.
